title: HeritageFaith Scripture Context Atlas + Seven-Leaf Commentary
purpose: Build a detailed, source-labeled study companion around HeritageFaith Scripture without changing the source text.
page_model: Each Scripture reference can own seven expandable commentary leaves. Seven is a research structure, not a hard word count.
exact_edition_boundary: The built-in public Scripture layer and any customer-selected local documents remain distinct. Comparison texts are separate source layers.
red_letter: Jesus-word highlighting is a reversible annotation layer. Preserve source/authority and confidence; never alter the immutable Scripture source.

seven_leaves.name: Text + Translation
questions: What passage is on this Scripture passage?
How do KJV, Douay-Rheims, and the active source edition differ in wording?
Are there manuscript, textual, or translation issues?
seven_leaves.rule: Never silently replace the wording of the source Bible. Comparison texts are separate layers.

seven_leaves.name: Names + Language
questions: What do the book, person, place, and key-word names mean?
What Hebrew, Aramaic, Greek, or Latin forms matter?
Which etymologies are disputed?
seven_leaves.rule: Mark folk etymologies and uncertain derivations.

seven_leaves.name: People + Peoples + Relationships
questions: Who appears here?
What family, political, social, or religious relationships matter?
Which historical peoples/cultures are involved?
seven_leaves.rule: Use “peoples/cultures/ethnic groups” rather than projecting modern racial categories backward unless a source specifically justifies the term.

seven_leaves.name: Places + Maps + Environment
questions: Where are the places?
How certain are proposed identifications?
What terrain, climate, roads, water, distances, and political boundaries matter?
seven_leaves.rule: Show alternate location hypotheses and confidence.

seven_leaves.name: Objects + Institutions + Daily Life
questions: What tools, foods, crops, animals, clothing, coins, buildings, offices, laws, rituals, and technologies appear?
What would they look and feel like in their period?

seven_leaves.name: Timeline + Historical Setting
questions: Where does this fit in biblical narrative time?
What conventional historical dates are proposed?
Which rulers, empires, wars, migrations, and temple periods overlap?
seven_leaves.rule: Use ranges and confidence instead of false precision.

seven_leaves.name: Theology + Interpretations + Resolution
questions: What is the passage doing in its literary context?
What Catholic teaching is relevant?
What Jewish, patristic, ecumenical, or historical-critical readings differ?
What questions remain unresolved?
What can a church group discuss or practice?
seven_leaves.rule: Label traditions and viewpoints. Do not turn one interpretive school into unqualified historical fact.

source_rule: For finished commentary, aim for at least three independent source families where available and preserve disagreements.
study_role: Curator, researcher, mapper, indexer, timeline keeper, citation checker, and explainer. The study layer does not invent missing evidence and does not overwrite the source Bible.
